routing.reason: A small feature with testable criteria that touches the API, a migration, the page and the docs, so it is more than one role's area.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, not `direct` — the change spans back-end (migration, API validation, tests) and front-end (page and add form), so it is not in one role's area — cost if wrong: a slightly longer run with a plan gate.

Ruling: product owner step left on at low effort — the ticket lists testable criteria, but the step is cheap and may surface edge cases (PATCH with null versus a missing field, date validation) — cost if wrong: a few cents spent repeating the criteria.

Ruling: PM, architect, UX and SEO skipped — the request is a small, well-specified field on an existing page and form, with no new flow, no cross-cutting decision and no public page — cost if wrong: the form's date field may need a small UI polish pass.

Ruling: security review at low effort — the only new input is a validated date string bound through a prepared statement, with no authentication, payments, personal data or secrets involved — cost if wrong: a missed validation gap, which the tests for criterion 3 should catch.

Ruling: note for the plan — PATCH must tell a missing `due_date` (keep it) from `null` (clear it); the existing `changes.x ?? task.x` pattern in `src/tasks.ts` would not clear it, so use a presence check (`'due_date' in body`). Validation must reject real-calendar misses such as 2026-02-30 and formats such as 2026-1-5 — cost if wrong: criterion 2 or 3 fails in review.

Ruling: the migration is a new entry appended to `migrations` in `src/db.ts` (`ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT`), never an edit of the shipped one; the dba review runs on it — cost if wrong: existing databases break.

Ruling: budget $1.00 — covers the framing, a short plan, two small tasks, the checks, a review round, the security review and the dba review on a ~275-line project — cost if wrong: the run stops before its reviews and needs a top-up.

criteria.why: Task and Row gain due_date (string|null); the column is nullable with no default, so it reads as null and is returned by every read path.
POST passes an optional due_date; PATCH uses `"due_date" in body` so null clears it and an absent key keeps the value.
isValidDueDate checks the regex and round-trips the date, which rejects 2026-1-5, tomorrow, 2026-02-30 and non-strings. It answers 400 with the exact message, and validation runs before any write.
A new migration `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT` is appended, and old rows get NULL. A test covers it, though it relies on `migrate` being exported.
app.js renders a <time> element with the due date next to the title, and index.html adds an optional date input that is sent only when filled.
The new tests cover create, default, PATCH set, clear and keep, invalid values, and the migration. The README documents the field and the error.

findings.what: The test imports `migrate` from ../src/db.ts, but the diff only adds an export for `migrations`. If `migrate` is not already exported, the ESM import fails and the whole test file breaks. I can't confirm either way from the diff.
`const filter =document.querySelector(...)` was reformatted, which is a stray whitespace change on a line the ticket didn't need touched.

The submit handler gains try/catch error display, and index.html gains flex-wrap and min-width CSS. This is reasonable, because a 400 would otherwise be an unhandled rejection, but it goes slightly beyond the ticket.

PATCH validates due_date before checking that the task exists, so an invalid date on an unknown id returns 400 rather than 404. This is defensible and tested. `"due_date" in body` would throw on a non-object JSON body and give a 500, though the existing body.title access already behaved that way.
`Parameters<typeof tasks.updateTask>[2]` is an awkward way to type `changes`. An exported type would be clearer.

judge.summary: The diff meets all six criteria. It has solid validation, a clean migration, and thorough tests for set, clear, keep, invalid values and migration. The main risk is that the test imports `migrate`, which the diff doesn't visibly export. There is also a small stray whitespace change in app.js.
